## Test 1 : animation CSS (rebond)

<style>
.balle {
  width: 60px;
  height: 60px;
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #e74c3c, #c0392b);
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: rebond 1s infinite alternate ease-in;
  margin: 20px 0;
}
@keyframes rebond {
  from { transform: translateY(0); }
  to   { transform: translateY(80px); }
}

.defile {
  animation: glisse 3s infinite alternate ease-in-out;
  font-size: 1.5em;
  font-weight: bold;
  color: #2c7fb8;
}
@keyframes glisse {
  from { transform: translateX(0); }
  to   { transform: translateX(200px); }
}

.pulse {
  display: inline-block;
  padding: 10px 20px;
  background: #27ae60;
  color: white;
  border-radius: 8px;
  animation: pulse 1.5s infinite;
}
@keyframes pulse {
  0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
  50%      { transform: scale(1.15); }
}
</style>

<div class="balle"></div>

<div class="defile">➜ Ce texte doit glisser de gauche à droite</div>

<br>

<div class="pulse">Ce bouton doit pulser</div>

## Test 2 : animation JavaScript (compteur)

<div id="compteur" style="font-size: 3em; font-weight: bold; color: #8e44ad;">0</div>

<script>
let n = 0;
setInterval(function() {
  n = (n + 1) % 101;
  document.getElementById("compteur").textContent = n;
}, 50);
</script>

## Test 3 : animation matplotlib (GIF embarqué)

Si vous voyez un graphique animé ci-dessous, Python + Quarto fonctionnent :

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Une sinusoïde animée"
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.animation import FuncAnimation
from IPython.display import HTML

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
line, = ax.plot(x, np.sin(x))
ax.set_ylim(-1.5, 1.5)

def update(frame):
    line.set_ydata(np.sin(x + frame / 10))
    return line,

anim = FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=60, blit=True)
plt.close(fig)
HTML(anim.to_jshtml())
```
